title: Request Guardian: lightweight request-tracing shim for cross-protocol propagation and sampling heuristics
creator: Priya Rao
description:
Problem: Multiple Redwood services (HTTP, gRPC, websocket workers, and background job queues) lose the request-level tracing metadata during handoffs and when requests are transformed (e.g., internal batchers, async job enqueue). This leads to fragmented traces, low trace completion rates for low-latency p99 paths, and poor sampling fidelity for high-volume batch workloads.

Goal: Implement a small, low-risk SDK/middleware shim — 'Request Guardian' — that provides:
- deterministic request fingerprinting to help stitch partial traces across protocol boundaries,
- a minimal, stable propagation header that coexists with existing W3C Trace Context,
- a pluggable adaptive sampling hook so Edge/ingress services can sample consistently for business-critical routes, and
- safe worker/queue handoff helpers that keep spans attached to the originating request id without leaking PII.

Non-goals: Replacing W3C Trace Context, deep OTEL rework, or changing backend storage or indexing. This is a runtime/SDK-layer shim for better signal quality and sampling alignment across heterogeneous transports.
acceptance_criteria: SDK middleware available for node/python/go with identical header name and semantics
End-to-end trace stitching rate for 'file-upload' and 'search' flows improves by >=30% on staging traces sampled at 1%
Adaptive sampling hook exposes route and cost signals and when enabled produces consistent sample decisions across services
No PII ever serialized in the Request Guardian header (automated scan/CI check passes)
Integration tests for HTTP->job-queue->worker handoff show propagated request_id and span markers
tasks: Implement node sdk middleware and express/fastify adapters (pkg: @redwood/request-guardian)
Implement python wsgi/async middleware for flask/fastapi
Add go http middleware and gRPC interceptor
Add queue helper for common job libraries (kafka producer header mapping, redis list marshaller)
Create CI checks to block PII in header values (regexp scanner)
End-to-end e2e playbook and staging run against observability staging cluster
Add dashboard panel for 'trace stitch rate' and sampling consistency per-route
updates: 2026-02-10 — Priya Rao: Created ticket and uploaded initial spec draft to Confluence. Identified three priority flows (file-upload, search, customer-webhooks).

2026-02-11 — Evan McClure: Completed prototype for node middleware that injects X-RW-Request header and a deterministic 64-bit fingerprint derived from method+path+user-agent. PoC PR opened: sdk#1453.
2026-02-12 — Security review (Kort Nguyen): flagged potential leak via query params; added blocker task to canonicalize and hash route fingerprints without raw query values.

2026-02-13 — Performance check (Miguel Ortega): microbenchmarks show ~120ns median overhead for header attach on Node 18 and ~200ns on Go net/http. Within SLO. Added an optimization to precompute fingerprint in ingress edge proxy.
2026-02-14 — UX/Observability (Asha Patel): dashboard panel sketched in Grafana. Proposed metrics: trace_stitch_rate, sampled_request_consistency, guardian_injection_error_rate.

2026-02-16 — Evan McClure: Started python/worker queue helper. Added e2e test scaffolding that replays a HTTP request into a redis queue consumer to validate propagation. Test currently flakes in CI due to timing; investigating backpressure handling.
review_feedback: PM (Jonah Silva): Prefer header name 'X-RW-REQ' to keep length small and avoid collision with future W3C fields.
Security (Kort Nguyen): Require deterministic hashing with env-specific salt and ensure salt rotation plan documented.
Infra (Lena Fischer): Suggest putting sampling decision into header as a single bit to avoid re-evaluation in downstream stateless workers.
Observability (Asha Patel): Add a dashboard that compares span counts with and without guardian header to prove benefit; want historical baseline ingest for 7d.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Header size growth could impact HTTP proxies. Mitigation: keep payload <= 64 bytes; use compact base36 fingerprint + 1-bit flags.
Risk: Different languages compute fingerprint differently. Mitigation: publish reference implementation in core-utils and add cross-lang unit tests
Risk: Sampling inconsistency across services. Mitigation: provide opt-in adaptive sampling hook and edge decision propagation; default to legacy sampling until rollout completes.
rollout_plan: Stage 0: SDK middleware in canary services only; guardian header disabled by default (feature flag).
Stage 1: Enable header inject at edge for non-sensitive routes; collect metrics for 72h and validate stitch rates in staging.
Stage 2: Gradual enable for high-value production routes (search, file-upload) behind kill-switch and monitor guard_injection_error_rate.
Stage 3: Enable adaptive sampling hook for teams that opt-in; document migration guide and SDK upgrade steps.
notes: Keep the shim intentionally small: user-land SDK is ~200 lines per language for maintainability.
Do not alter persisted trace IDs in storage; Request Guardian only adds a secondary request fingerprint and sampling hints.
Coordinate with infra team to add header allowlist for internal proxies (ENG-61234)
